handback.title: A settings file picks each role's agent and model
handback.summary: One settings file says which agent and model the planner, worker and reviewer use; Kimi is supported first, then Codex.
handback.feature: The owner picks each role's agent and model in one settings file. Stories: (1) the file; (2) runs follow it, on Kimi; (3) Codex.

stories.title: One settings file names each role's agent and model
stories.user_story: The owner sets each role's agent and model in one small file at the top of the repo.
stories.context: Today the agent and model are fixed in the agent workflow: it installs Claude Code and runs it with a model set once for every role (.github/workflows/agent.yml, the MODEL line and the claude -p step). No settings file exists. PyYAML is not installed and the repo adds no dependencies, so the file is read by a small reader of its own; the tests' own YAML reader (tests/test_start.py, load_yaml) shows the subset the workflows need. Story 2 wires the file into runs; this story only adds the file and its reader.

acceptance_criteria.text: The settings file is a YAML file, so the owner edits plain keys and values.
acceptance_criteria.words: The file is YAML-like, a structured file.

acceptance_criteria.text: The planner, the worker and the reviewer each get their own agent and model in the file.
acceptance_criteria.words: Any agent, any model: planner, worker and reviewer each pick theirs.

acceptance_criteria.text: A role may name any model its agent takes; Dokima keeps no list of allowed models.
Moving a role to another subscription is a one-line edit: that role's line in the file.
acceptance_criteria.words: It exposes a simple interface for deciding the orchestration across subscriptions.

non_functional.text: The roles sit in their own section of the file, so other settings can join later.
non_functional.why: The owner expects the file to hold other settings later.
non_functional.words: Later it may expand into other settings.

stories.title: Each run follows the settings file, starting with Kimi
stories.user_story: Each role runs on the agent and model the owner set, and Kimi works first.
stories.context: The agent workflow runs Claude Code with one fixed model and then fails the run when the session logs name any other model (.github/workflows/agent.yml, the step 'Fail closed on a bad hand-back or the wrong model'; dokima/agent_records.py, models_used and run_report read Claude's logs and claude.json). Running Kimi needs the workflow changed, Kimi's command line installed and a Kimi key added as a secret by the owner; the model check and the run's stats must read Kimi's logs too. AGENTS.md forbids workflow changes unless the issue asks; see the owner question on this.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each run starts the agent and model the settings file gives its role.
acceptance_criteria.words: A settings file decides which agent and model each role uses, across subscriptions.

acceptance_criteria.text: A role set to Kimi runs on Kimi, with the model the file names.
Dokima's own settings file names Kimi for every role, so its credit is used first.
acceptance_criteria.words: Kimi first, since I want to use up its credit

stories.title: A role can run on Codex
stories.user_story: The owner can move any role to Codex by naming it in the settings file.
stories.context: Built after Kimi, as the owner ordered. It reuses story 2's way of starting an agent from the settings file; it adds Codex's command line, its key as a secret, and reading Codex's logs for the model check and the run's stats (dokima/agent_records.py). Open issue 39 plans one adapter per agent, Codex among them.

acceptance_criteria.text: A role set to Codex runs on Codex, with the model the file names.

raises.label: Two readings
raises.text: Does Kimi first mean build Kimi first, or switch to Codex once Kimi's credit runs out? Plan assumes building.
raises.evidence: The issue says 'Kimi first, since I want to use up its credit, then Codex' and names no fallback.

raises.label: Workflow change needed
raises.text: Kimi and Codex need the agent workflow changed and their keys added. May the stories do that? Plan assumes yes.
raises.evidence: `.github/workflows/agent.yml` fixes `MODEL: claude-opus-5-5` and runs `claude -p`; AGENTS.md forbids workflow changes unless the issue asks.

raises.label: Doubt: overlaps open issue
raises.text: Issue 39 also plans one adapter per agent. Should this issue build the Kimi and Codex ones? Plan assumes so.
raises.evidence: #39 asks for 'One small adapter per agent (Claude Code, Codex, others)'.
